intro: If you have searched for an independent tax advisor near me, you are probably looking for someone local who can look at your tax affairs without the layers of a large firm. Perhaps you have a specific question, a return that has become complicated, or a letter from HMRC you would rather not handle alone. iComply is a free introduction service: you tell us what you need, and we introduce you to a suitable UK tax professional who quotes you directly, with the price on application.
need_heading: What people searching for an independent tax advisor near me usually need
need_lead: Most people behind this search want a straightforward conversation with someone who can take responsibility for their tax position.
needs: You are self-employed or run a small business and want an adviser who will deal with your tax affairs personally rather than passing you between departments.
You have received a letter or enquiry from HMRC and want someone local to go through it with you and explain what is being asked.
Your circumstances have changed, perhaps through a house sale, an inheritance or time spent working abroad, and you want to understand the tax consequences before you act.
You have been using an accountant for years but feel your tax questions are not getting the specialist attention they deserve.
You want to check that your returns and records are in order, and you would prefer to sit down with an independent adviser near you rather than work entirely remotely.
context_heading: What independent means when it comes to tax advice
context: "Tax adviser" is not a protected title in the UK, so anyone can use it. The main specialist bodies are the Chartered Institute of Taxation, whose members hold the CTA qualification, and the Association of Taxation Technicians, whose members hold the ATT qualification. Many accountants and solicitors also advise on tax, and members of these bodies follow Professional Conduct in Relation to Taxation, a shared code covering honesty, confidentiality and dealing with HMRC.

Tax advisers who charge a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, and HMRC has been tightening standards for paid tax agents. It is therefore reasonable to ask about qualifications, supervision and professional indemnity insurance before you go ahead. Independent advisers work outside the large firms, which often means partner-level attention and a specialist focus, and they may cost less for focused work.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the tax issue in your own words, including whether it is about income tax, self assessment, capital gains, inheritance tax or something else.
Say whether you are self-employed, a company director, a landlord, retired or employed, as this shapes the kind of adviser you need.
Mention whether HMRC has already been in touch and, if so, what the letter or enquiry is about.
Explain whether you already have an accountant and whether you are looking to change or simply add specialist help.
Say how near you would like the adviser to be, and whether you are happy with video or telephone meetings as well as face to face.
Include any deadlines you are working towards, such as a return that is due or a response HMRC has asked for.
questions: Which professional bodies do you belong to, and what qualifications do you hold?
How would you describe your specialist experience with the kind of tax issue I have described?
Will you be the person dealing with my affairs, or will the work be passed to someone else?
Are you supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, and do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
How do you charge for your work, and can you explain what the quote will cover?
If my issue needs a solicitor or another specialist, do you have a network you can draw on?

faqs.q: Is an independent tax adviser different from an accountant?
faqs.a: The two roles overlap, and many accountants advise on tax. An independent tax adviser usually works outside the large firms and may focus specifically on tax rather than on accounts and bookkeeping. What matters most is that the person has the qualifications and experience for your particular issue.

faqs.q: How do I judge whether an adviser is right for me?
faqs.a: Ask about their qualifications and the professional bodies they belong to, their experience with your type of issue, and how they charge. A short initial conversation should tell you whether they listen carefully and explain things clearly. You are entitled to ask about supervision and insurance before you commit.

faqs.q: Can iComply tell me what my tax position is?
faqs.a: No. iComply is an introduction service and does not give professional advice. We take the details of what you need and introduce you to a suitable UK tax professional, who will discuss your situation and quote you directly.

faqs.q: What if I am not sure whether I need a tax adviser at all?
faqs.a: Describe your situation to us as fully as you can, including what prompted you to look. The professional you are introduced to can tell you whether their help is needed and what it would involve. You are under no obligation to go ahead once you have the quote.
